MIS.metrics: percent of posts containing a climate denial stance
MIS.metrics_desc: “This indicates that a majority of the tweets are likely to support climate change, corroborating our annotation with suggests that only about 16% of the tweets deny the issue.” ([Sadik et al., 2022, p. 2])

MIS.findings:
“Supporters stress the imminence of climate change, and deniers deflect it with conspiracy theories, and alternative explanations.” ([Sadik et al., 2022, p. 1]

POL.type: interactional polarization (tendency to interact with like-minded individuals and disengage with those that hold opposing views)
POL.measure: stance-label distribution | network descriptive statistics | user/account statistics
POL.findings:
“Tweets supporting climate change are shared from verified accounts, and are liked and retweeted many times, whereas those denying climate change circulate through close, like-minded communities.” ([Sadik et al., 2022, p. 1])
There is “significant politicization of the climate change debate, with each side blaming the other. Supporters chide deniers for ignoring the urgent threat, and skeptics question the motives and scientific evidence advanced by the supporters.” ([Sadik et al., 2022, p. 7]
MOT.motiv_cite:
“Social media platforms such as Facebook and Twitter are tightly knit into the fabric of our modern society. People often turn to these social platforms to voice their instantaneous and unbridled thoughts and opinions on a variety of topics; ranging from many routine matters such as reviews of products and services to polarized, hot-button issues including universal health care, gun control, religious freedom, etc.” ([Sadik et al., 2022, p. 1]
“It then becomes necessary to identify these skeptics and understand their reasons to deny an issue that appears nearly settled with scientific evidence. This can guide us in designing educational initiatives to dispel their misconceptions, in the hope to bring all of us on the same page to mitigate this existential threat.” ([Sadik et al., 2022, p. 1]
“This debate on climate change is particularly resurrected during high-profile natural disasters such as a blizzard, extreme heat and temperatures, hurricanes, floods, fires and snowstorms, which have a significant economic impact” ([Sadik et al., 2022, p. 1])
